input.quote: The Servicer will indemnify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (including in its capacity as Note Paying Agent), and their officers, directors, employees and agents (each, an "Indemnified Person") for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees and expenses) resulting from the Servicer's (including in its capacity as Custodian) willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents
input.rationale: Section 6.3 (p0288-p0299) is a counterparty-side indemnity that runs in our favour: Cellco as Servicer and as Marketing Agent indemnifies the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee (and their officers, directors, employees and agents) for wilful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, uncapped, with claim-notice that is not forfeited absent prejudice (p0293), Servicer-funded defence including separate counsel on conflict (p0294), and survival of termination (p0298). That covers the misconduct, notice and control-of-defence elements of the preferred position. It does not, however, contain an IP-infringement indemnity, a breach-of-law or data-breach limb, or an express duty to defend, so on a literal reading it fails the fallback. We are escalating rather than redlining because (i) this is a receivables transfer and servicing agreement with no services, deliverables, software or IP licence anywhere in the document (searches for intellectual property, licence, software and trademark return nothing), so an IP-infringement/procure-modify-replace-refund construct is inapposite; and (ii) the two remaining fallback/preferred elements would each cut against us - the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap would newly cap an indemnity that is presently uncapped, and the preferred "Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law" element would introduce an Issuer/Depositor indemnity where the Agreement currently imposes none. The only genuinely value-adding gaps are an express duty to defend and a data-breach limb covering Obligor data the Servicer/Custodian handles; we recommend a business decision on whether to pursue those before any operative change. Depositor's defence of title in Section 9.2 (p0372) is a separate, narrow title covenant and is not responsive to this rule.

mappings.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
mappings.explanation: Section 6.3(b) gives the Servicer/Marketing Agent an option ('may participate in and assume the defense'), not a duty to defend; defence costs are reimbursed under 6.3(a). Adding a hard defence duty is a live ask but we have not drafted it pending the business decision described in the rationale.

mappings.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
mappings.quote: The Servicer will indemnify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee

mappings.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
mappings.explanation: The Agreement involves no services, deliverables, software or IP licence (no hits for intellectual property, licence, software or trademark), so an IP-infringement limb has no subject matter here; we have not inserted one without instructions.

mappings.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
mappings.explanation: Section 6.3 is limited to wilful misconduct, bad faith and gross negligence; a breach-of-Law limb is absent. Section 6.1 contains only a no-violation-of-Law representation qualified by Material Adverse Effect (p0281), which is not an indemnity.

mappings.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
mappings.explanation: No unauthorised-access/disclosure limb exists, although Cellco as Servicer and Custodian handles Obligor account and Receivable File data. Flagged for a business decision rather than unilaterally drafted.

mappings.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
mappings.quote: willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents

mappings.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
mappings.quote: promptly notify the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable, of the Proceeding

mappings.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
mappings.quote: The Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable, may participate in and assume the defense and settlement of a Proceeding at its expense.

mappings.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
mappings.explanation: Section 6.3 imposes no cooperation covenant on the Indemnified Person. Its absence is neutral-to-favourable to us, so we have not volunteered one.

mappings.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
mappings.explanation: The Agreement contains no Issuer or Depositor indemnity in Cellco's favour at all, so the element is satisfied in substance but there is no verbatim text to cite; drafting any Customer-side indemnity would weaken our position.
